Summary (auto):
Quick weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark numbers — p50/p95 latency and throughput vs the customer's baseline provider. Discussed tuning knobs (batching, KV caching, quantization), infra differences, and next steps for a final comparison run. Agreed on a few action items and deeper kernel/deployment review.

Topics:
- Baseline provider vs Redwood runs
- p50/p95 latency deltas and tail behavior
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and sustained RPS
- Batching/auto-batching configuration and tradeoffs
- KV/prefix cache impacts on conversational workloads
- Quantization profiles and accuracy regressions
- Security/compliance asks (SOC2, KMS)

Transcript:
00:00 Ethan: all right hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um let's kick off, quick agenda is benchmarks then tuning then actions 00:12 Sanjay: yeah that's great, we only have 45 so i'd love to get straight into the numbers 00:18 Maya: cool i'll share my screen in a sec, but top line: across the test suite this week redwood p50 improved vs baseline by ~25% and p95 by ~18 but there were a couple of outliers on long context flows 00:34 Laura: when you say baseline which provider is that again? 00:38 Maya: it's the customer's current managed endpoint, listed internally as "baseline-cloud" - which is on CloudVendorX with their standard 4xA100ish setup, although the infra config is a bit different 00:48 Sanjay: yeah baseline-cloud is what we run in prod, we liked the early numbers but tail spikes worry us 00:55 Maya: right, so p50 numbers: baseline p50 110ms token generation average for the text-gen model on 2k context, redwood p50 ~82ms. p95 baseline 420ms, redwood 345ms, those are from the mixed prompt suite 01:18 Diego: quick note, transcription may show values slightly off, but logs are attached in the sheet 01:24 Oliver: what's the throughput like? tokens per second, sustained? 01:29 Maya: baseline sustained tokens/sec ~6.8k on their cluster for single-stream higher concurrency it's lower, redwood sustained ~8.5k under same request mix 01:39 Marta: what's the concurrency pattern you used for that number? 01:43 Maya: we ran 40 concurrent connections, batching target size 8, auto-batching enabled on Redwood runtime, baseline used manual batching on their endpoint 01:54 Sanjay: the baseline does per-request batching too but we've seen that it sometimes fails to coalesce, so tail gets worse 01:59 Maya: yeah that's one of the big diffs - our continuous batching and prefix-KV reuse helps reduce compute for repetition, in the transcription sometimes shows K-V cash which is wrong 02:12 Laura: any accuracy regressions with quantization? you mentioned q4 earlier 02:17 Maya: we tested int8-ish q4_0 profile on one model - minimal regression on our evals (delta less than 0.6% on rouge/rouge-like metrics) but for safety we recommended floating for their highest-sensitivity flows 02:30 Sanjay: can you repeat the outlier case you mentioned? which prompt triggers tail latency 02:35 Maya: it's mainly multi-turn with long shared context + a lot of retrieval hits, the p99 shot up to ~1.6s on two tests - we traced that to a cold KV cache + kernel fallback in one pod 02:49 Ethan: yeah we saw a kernel fallback when the sequence length exploded - it fell back to a slower kernel path, we logged that as a perf event 02:56 Marta: is that something you can fix quickly or is that a model/infra limitation? 03:01 Maya: it's a bit of both - we can tune kernel selection thresholds and pre-split the big sequences, and also advise a small change in how you pack prompts. maya: also we can pin a different kernel that avoids fallback at the expense of slight per-token throughput 03:18 Laura: what's the impact on cost if you pin that kernel or disable quantization? 03:23 Ethan: good question - in the sheet we had run-level cost estimates. ballpark: pinning the fallback-avoider kernel increases cost ~12% but improves p99 by ~40% in that scenario; disabling q4 raises cost ~18-22% for that model 03:40 Sanjay: ok that's within the window if it stabilizes tails for our SLAs, we need to see the per-route numbers though 03:46 Maya: agreed, we'll add per-route p95/p99 and token-count cost to the spreadsheet 03:51 Diego: note that our console can show token-level cost by route so you can reconcile real traffic later 03:57 Oliver: any security blockers? we need SOC2 and KMS integration for keys 04:02 Ethan: we have SOC2 type II available, and KMS/HSM integrations - we'll share the docs after the call 04:08 Marta: are audit logs enabled on private deployments? 04:11 Ethan: yes, private (VPC) has full audit logs and longer retention options; we can include log samples in the pack 04:18 Laura: on the baseline runs, were you able to reproduce their infra exactly? i'm worried about apples-to-apples 04:24 Maya: we attempted to match CPU/GPU generation and model config; baseline has slightly different CUDA/kdriver versions and we called that out in the notes - ctrl they had a different kernel build which explained some of the variance 04:38 Sanjay: so next step is a final head-to-head where we both run the same harness with the same seed and batch setup? 04:44 Maya: yes, we proposed identical harness: same prompt seed, same batching (2x batch), and a new run where baseline turns on their auto-coalesce, that should highlight the real diff 04:56 Marta: i can run the baseline harness on our side if you give the test runner and the exact config 05:00 Maya: i'll drop the runner config in the folder after this call 05:04 Ethan: can we talk about the per-model rollout? customer wants stepwise canary to prod 05:09 Laura: yes product team likes canary then full roll; what's your recommendation on size? 05:13 Maya: typical is 5% canary for latency-sensitive endpoints for 48-72 hours then 25% then full; we also suggest A/B on quality metrics to detect regressions 05:27 Sanjay: related question: if we go with Redwood Dedicated vs hosted, what changes in latency/cost? 05:33 Ethan: Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and lower variance - cost is higher on committed base but unit token cost drops at scale; hosted is simpler to operate 05:44 Laura: any notes on private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for compliance? 05:48 Ethan: private deployment supports VPC and on-prem packaging - there is an enterprise license and support cost, we'll attach pricing sheet 05:56 Oliver: can you reiterate the biggest wins we saw this week? 06:00 Maya: p50 improved ~25%, sustained tokens/sec up ~25%, p95 improved ~18% across mixed suite; one p99 outlier remains tied to kernel fallback and cold KV cache 06:12 Sanjay: ok that's useful, i'm concerned about the flaky tail - can you prioritise a fix? 06:16 Maya: yes we'll prioritize kernel selection tuning and also provide packing guidance to reduce sequence length spikes 06:23 Diego: i'll also open an internal ticket with engineering and link it to this POC so we can track 06:29 Ethan: perfect, any final questions?
